zoledronic-acid.name: Zoledronic acid
zoledronic-acid.explanation: Zoledronic acid binds to bone and reduces the activity of cells that break bone down. In selected people with early breast cancer it forms part of the adjuvant plan. It does not replace surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy or endocrine treatment.
zoledronic-acid.watch: Report jaw pain or a wound that will not heal, reduced urine, muscle cramps, eye pain or new thigh/groin pain.
risks: Flu-like reaction and muscle or joint pain
Rare atypical thigh fracture or eye inflammation

talazoparib.name: Talazoparib
talazoparib.mechanism: Disrupts DNA repair in BRCA-associated cancer
talazoparib.explanation: Talazoparib inhibits PARP and traps it on damaged DNA. Cancer cells with inherited BRCA1/2 changes may have less ability to repair this damage. Normal bone marrow can also be affected, so blood-count monitoring is essential.
visual: BRCA-deficient cells less able to repair
talazoparib.watch: Report fever, infections, unusual bruising, persistent fatigue or breathlessness.
risks: Anaemia, low white cells and platelets
Rare serious bone-marrow disorders including MDS/AML

neratinib.name: Neratinib
neratinib.mechanism: Blocks growth signalling inside HER2-positive cancer cells
neratinib.explanation: Neratinib binds irreversibly to signalling enzymes in the HER family, including HER2. It is used after trastuzumab-based adjuvant therapy in a specific hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-positive early-breast setting. Its effects on the bowel make early diarrhoea prevention important.
neratinib.watch: Start the prescribed diarrhoea-prevention plan with the first dose. Report diarrhoea early, especially poor intake, dizziness or reduced urine.

atezolizumab.name: Atezolizumab
atezolizumab.explanation: Atezolizumab blocks PD-L1 signalling that can restrain immune cells. This may help the immune system attack cancer, but it can also inflame healthy organs. Immune effects can begin during treatment or after it has stopped.
atezolizumab.watch: Report new cough, diarrhoea, jaundice, severe rash, unusual weakness, headache, thirst or changes in urination promptly.
risks: Immune inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver or kidneys
Thyroid, adrenal or pituitary problems and diabetes
Rare serious heart, nerve or muscle inflammation
Infusion reactions and severe skin reactions

00545.title: Zoledronic acid · adjuvant breast treatment
00545.setting: Adjuvant breast cancer · postmenopausal (natural or treatment-induced)
00545.schedule: Zoledronic acid by IV infusion once every six months for up to five years, unless progression or unacceptable toxicity changes the plan. The usual source dose is 4 mg, with renal review before prescribing.
00545.why: This may be added to an adjuvant plan after discussing recurrence risk, menopause status, kidney function, dental health and the expected benefit. It is a separate treatment from medicines used to control bone metastases.
00545.purpose: Reduce recurrence risk as part of the agreed early-breast treatment plan.
00545.blood: Before starting: renal profile, magnesium, calcium and phosphate. Check creatinine before every infusion; compare it with baseline as well as reviewing creatinine clearance. Correct low calcium and review vitamin D.
00545.other_checks: Complete a dental assessment and preventive care before treatment where appropriate. Report dental symptoms; discuss invasive dental work with oncology and dental teams. Hydration is individualised, especially with heart failure.
00545.urgent: Report jaw pain, exposed bone or a non-healing mouth wound, reduced urine, tingling or muscle spasms, painful red eyes, or new thigh/groin pain.
patient_support: Calcium and vitamin D
Follow the prescribed daily supplements; the team checks calcium and adjusts them if it is high or low.
Dental care
Keep routine dental care and tell the dentist about treatment. Report jaw pain or a wound that does not heal.
Flu-like symptoms
Aches or fever can occur after infusion. Use the agreed symptom plan; seek advice if severe or persistent.
Hydration
Follow the team’s fluid advice; heart or kidney problems may change it.
00545.line: Adjuvant treatment in the eligible postmenopausal breast population; not a metastatic bone schedule.
00545.alternatives: Discuss biomarker-directed, endocrine, chemotherapy and supportive-care options appropriate to this setting, including the option not to proceed.

Review organ function, current medicines, toxicity history and patient priorities.

clinical_cautions: NCCP marks adjuvant use off-label; follow local consent/governance.
Do not substitute osteoporosis or metastatic bone dosing schedules.
Baseline creatinine exactly 124 µmol/L and fractional CrCl gaps need explicit review.

00545.interactions: Check new prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines and supplements with the oncology pharmacist before taking them.
00545.after: Keep the agreed follow-up and report persistent or new symptoms between visits.
00545.consent: Discuss the adjuvant off-label indication, renal risk, hypocalcaemia, jaw osteonecrosis, rare atypical fracture and alternatives. Record menopause status and the agreed duration.
00545.support_summary: Review renal function, calcium, vitamin D, dental health and hydration before each infusion.

00605.title: Talazoparib · breast monotherapy
00605.setting: Germline BRCA1/2-mutated, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
00605.schedule: Talazoparib is taken once daily continuously until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The usual starting dose is 1 mg; kidney function, interactions and side effects can require a different prescription.
00605.why: Talazoparib targets a DNA-repair vulnerability associated with inherited BRCA1/2 changes. Suitability also depends on HER2 status, previous anthracycline/taxane treatment and, for hormone-receptor-positive disease, previous endocrine treatment or its suitability.
00605.purpose: Control advanced cancer and symptoms while balancing side effects and treatment burden.
00605.blood: Check FBC, kidney and liver function before starting and every four weeks. More frequent blood review may be needed for low counts; prolonged abnormalities require specialist assessment.
00605.other_checks: Confirm the germline BRCA result and previous treatment. Review pregnancy status and contraception, kidney function and interacting medicines, particularly P-glycoprotein inhibitors.
00605.urgent: Contact oncology urgently for fever, shivers, infection, unusual bleeding, marked fatigue or new breathlessness.
patient_support: Blood counts
Keep four-weekly blood reviews and any additional tests. Fever or unusual bleeding needs prompt advice.
Taking capsules
Use the strength and number on your current prescription. Do not replace a missed or vomited dose.
Nausea
Use the prescribed rescue plan; call if vomiting affects fluids or tablets.
Medicines review
Check every new medicine or supplement with the oncology pharmacist.

00605.alternatives: Discuss biomarker-directed, endocrine, chemotherapy and supportive-care options appropriate to this setting, including the option not to proceed.

00720.title: Neratinib · extended adjuvant treatment
00720.setting: Hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-positive early breast cancer after adjuvant trastuzumab
00720.schedule: Neratinib is taken once daily with food for one year. The usual starting dose is 240 mg; the team may interrupt or reduce it for toxicity. Treatment starts less than one year after completing adjuvant trastuzumab.
00720.why: Neratinib is an extended adjuvant option for selected hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-positive early breast cancer after trastuzumab-based treatment. Expected benefit, prior HER2 therapy, bowel and liver health, other medicines and the burden of daily treatment guide the discussion.
00720.purpose: Reduce recurrence risk as part of the agreed early-breast treatment plan.
00720.blood: FBC monthly for the first six months, then every three months. Liver tests at week 1, monthly for the first three months, then every six weeks; test earlier for liver symptoms or significant diarrhoea.
00720.other_checks: Confirm normal baseline LVEF eligibility; cardiac/LVEF assessment is clinically indicated. Review bowel symptoms, hydration, weight and interacting medicines. Continue any follow-up already required after prior trastuzumab; neratinib does not reset that plan.
00720.urgent: Report diarrhoea early. Poor intake, dizziness, reduced urine, blood in stool, fever, severe pain or jaundice needs prompt clinical advice.
patient_support: Diarrhoea prevention
Have the prescribed loperamide plan ready before the first tablet. Call early if diarrhoea starts or worsens.
Hydration
Follow the fluid plan and report dizziness, poor intake or reduced urine.
Liver checks
Keep the week-1 and subsequent liver tests; report yellow skin, dark urine or severe nausea.
Other medicines
Check acid-suppressing medicines and all new prescriptions with the pharmacist.
00720.line: Extended adjuvant treatment, started less than one year after completing trastuzumab-based adjuvant treatment.
00720.alternatives: Discuss biomarker-directed, endocrine, chemotherapy and supportive-care options appropriate to this setting, including the option not to proceed.
selection_factors: Confirm cancer stage, receptor status, prior treatment and source eligibility.
Review organ function, current medicines, toxicity history and patient priorities.
Consider practical visits or adherence requirements, symptoms and patient preferences.
00720.limitations: Source availability does not make a regimen the preferred option for every person. Trial populations and schedules may differ from current care.
clinical_cautions: NCCP and EMA conflict on severe hepatic/renal impairment; the assessment flags specialist review and avoids an automatic dose.
The patient evidence discussion must reflect HR-positive/HER2-positive early disease and prior trastuzumab; it is not a metastatic schedule.

CONTROL dose escalation is supplementary tolerability evidence, not an automatic replacement of the NCCP v2 schedule.

00720.missed: Do not replace a missed dose. Contact the team about diarrhoea or a treatment hold; restart and dose reductions require their instructions.
00720.interactions: Avoid grapefruit, pomegranate and proton-pump inhibitors. If an H2 blocker is prescribed, take neratinib at least two hours before or ten hours after it; separate antacids by at least three hours. Check CYP3A/P-glycoprotein interactions with the pharmacist.
00720.after: Keep the agreed follow-up and report persistent or new symptoms between visits.
00720.consent: Discuss the exact setting, expected benefit, alternatives, medicine-specific risks, monitoring, contraception and urgent contact plan.
00720.support_summary: Prescribed loperamide from the first dose, early hydration and diarrhoea review, liver monitoring and an acid-suppression/interactions plan.

00688.title: Atezolizumab + nab-paclitaxel
00688.setting: Previously untreated unresectable locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer with eligible PD-L1 expression
00688.schedule: Atezolizumab 840 mg is given on Days 1 and 15, before nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m² on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Nab-paclitaxel is planned for up to six cycles; extension needs consultant review. Atezolizumab may continue after chemotherapy stops.
00688.why: This combination brings checkpoint immunotherapy together with albumin-bound paclitaxel for a defined first-line triple-negative breast population. The validated PD-L1 test, previous treatment, autoimmune history, organ health and patient priorities affect suitability.
00688.purpose: Control advanced cancer and symptoms while balancing side effects and treatment burden.
00688.blood: Baseline FBC, kidney/liver function, glucose, thyroid function, hepatitis B/C testing and morning cortisol. FBC, kidney/liver tests and glucose before each cycle; check the count results needed for Day 8 and Day 15 decisions.
00688.other_checks: Thyroid function at Cycle 1 Day 1 and every second cycle. Review immune symptoms throughout and after treatment. Cardiac imaging is based on history/prior anthracyclines or clinical concern; there is no routine HER2-style echo schedule.
00688.urgent: Fever, new cough or breathlessness, diarrhoea, severe rash, jaundice, unusual weakness, marked thirst, severe headache or confusion needs prompt advice, including after treatment ends.
patient_support: Know the treatment day
Day 8 is nab-paclitaxel only. Confirm which medicines are due at every visit.
Immune symptoms
Report new symptoms promptly, even after treatment ends. Do not assume diarrhoea or breathlessness is an ordinary chemotherapy effect.
Nerves and blood counts
Report numbness before the next dose; fever or unusual bleeding needs urgent advice.
Medicines and vaccines
Discuss steroids, new medicines and vaccinations with the team.
00688.line: First-line advanced TNBC with source-eligible PD-L1 immune-cell expression; confirm the validated assay and prior treatment.
00688.alternatives: Discuss biomarker-directed, endocrine, chemotherapy and supportive-care options appropriate to this setting, including the option not to proceed.
selection_factors: Confirm TNBC and PD-L1 immune-cell staining using the validated source assay; do not substitute CPS.
Check prior systemic treatment for metastatic disease and any disease-free-interval requirement.
Review autoimmune illness, immunosuppression, infection and organ function.

clinical_cautions: Do not substitute single-agent atezolizumab 1680 mg or another atezolizumab indication.
Nab-paclitaxel and solvent-based paclitaxel are not interchangeable in this regimen.

00738.title: Bevacizumab + weekly paclitaxel
00738.setting: First-line metastatic breast cancer · source-defined eligibility
00738.schedule: Bevacizumab 10 mg/kg is given on Days 1 and 15, with paclitaxel 80 mg/m² on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Continue according to benefit, toxicity and the treating team’s plan.
00738.why: Bevacizumab blocks VEGF-driven blood-vessel signalling while paclitaxel disrupts cell division. Treatment selection considers the first-line setting, cancer biology, alternatives and the balance between disease control and vascular, bleeding and nerve risks.
00738.purpose: Control advanced cancer and symptoms while balancing side effects and treatment burden.
00738.blood: Baseline FBC, kidney/liver tests and urine protein. Review blood counts, renal/liver function and urine protein before cycles; Day 8 FBC is explicitly required. Check current counts for each paclitaxel decision.
00738.other_checks: Measure blood pressure before each bevacizumab dose and follow the agreed urine-protein plan. Review bleeding, clotting, wounds and planned procedures. Cardiac imaging is considered for prior anthracycline/chest radiotherapy or clinical concern; warfarin requires additional INR monitoring.
00738.urgent: Seek urgent advice for major bleeding, severe headache or visual change, chest pain, breathlessness, one-sided weakness, severe abdominal pain, fever or poor wound healing.
patient_support: Blood pressure and urine
Attend the required checks even if you feel well. Report severe headache, visual change or swelling.
Operations and dental work
Tell oncology about planned procedures; bevacizumab timing and wound healing need review.
Paclitaxel premedicines
The first dose and later doses have different plans. A previous reaction changes the assessment.
Nerves and bleeding
Report numbness, unusual bleeding or bruising before the next visit.
